title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1981-82 programme of 'déploiement' of stratified spaces, announced without proof in Esquisse d'un programme. The aim is to show that a tame stratified space is equivalent to combinatorial-geometric data: manifolds with boundary or corners glued along proper submersions or fibrations. A 'stratified space' here is a space X with a family of closed sub-spaces (X_i) indexed by a poset I. These satisfy i<=j => X_i ⊂ X_j and X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k<=i,j} X_k. There are extra structures (B_α, Σ_α), α∈Λ, which are restricted along with everything else.

Inductive step (previous page). I_0 is a set of minimal indices. One chooses strict conical (tubular) neighbourhoods T_β of the X_β (β∈I_0), with T_{I_0} = ⊔ T_β. They are transverse to the (B_α, Σ_α), and the X_i with i∈I* = I∖I_0 are admissible for them. Then:
- if i is not >= β, X_i misses T_β;
- if i > β, then X_i ⊃ X_β and X_i ∩ T_β = I·(X_i ∩ Ṫ_β) ∪ X_β, i.e. a mapping cylinder.

This page, item (18): the reduced data. Cutting out the open tubes, one records:
- X* = X − T°_{I_0}, the complement of the open tubes;
- its boundary pieces Ẋ_β = Ṫ_β;
- the induced (B*_α, Σ*_α) = (B_α, Σ_α)|X*;
- the traces X*_i = X_i ∩ X* for i∈I*;
- the minimal strata X_β with their induced structures (B_{β,α}, Σ_{β,α}) = (B_α, Σ_α)|X_β;
- the projections p_β : Ẋ_β → X_β (the 'link bundles').

The margin calls (18) a 'système de cylindres-bord transversaux' (system of transverse boundary-cylinders).

Item (19): reconstruction from the data.
- X̂ = X* ⊔_{Ẋ} C(p): the original space is X* glued along Ẋ = ⊔ Ẋ_β to the mapping cylinder C(p) = ⊔_β C(p_β).
- T_β = C(p_β).
- X_β is clear for β∈I_0.
- For i∈I*, X_i = X*_i ∪ ⋃_β (I·Ẋ_{i,β} ∪ X_β), where Ẋ_{i,β} = X*_i ∩ Ẋ_β; that is, X*_i plus the mapping cylinder of p_β restricted to Ẋ_{i,β}.
- B_α = B*_α ∪ ⋃_β I·Ḃ_α, where Ḃ_α = B*_α ∩ Ẋ_β.
- Σ_α is obtained from Σ*_α and the (B_{β,α}, Σ_{β,α}).

Item (20): conditions on (18) making it 'admissible'.
- (a) The Ẋ_β are disjoint.
- (b) Each Ẋ_β is transverse to (B*_α, Σ*_α).
- (c) The maps (Ẋ_β, Ḃ_{βα}, Σ̇_{βα}) → (X_β, B_{β,α}, Σ_{β,α}) are transverse (a margin note seems to say 'or submersive'), where the dotted structure is induced from (B*_α, Σ*_α).
- (d) The X*_i are transverse to the system ((Ẋ_β, Σ_β), (B*_α, Σ*_α)).

Remark: (a) and (b) imply that the combined system of the Ẋ_β and the (B*_α, Σ*_α) is transverse.

Next page. Conditions (e) and (f) are added: monotonicity and the intersection law for the X*_i, encoded via I*_β = {i ≥ β}. Together these ensure that the reconstructed X_i form a stratification.

In modern terms: this is one step of the 'unzipping' or blow-up equivalence. A stratified space with control data corresponds to a manifold-with-boundary/corners X* together with fibrations from boundary faces onto lower strata. Applied inductively, it gives the equivalence between tame stratified spaces and 'déployé' data.
errors: In (19) the formula for X_i (i∈I*) takes the union over all β∈I_0 and adds X_β in each term. Literally this would put every minimal stratum X_β into X_i, even when i is not >= β (then Ẋ_{i,β} = ∅ and only X_β would be added), contradicting (15). The union should run over β∈I_0 with β<i. Equivalently, the term should be the mapping cylinder C(p_β|Ẋ_{i,β}), which contains X_β only when Ẋ_{i,β} is nonempty and p_β restricted to it is onto. Grothendieck wrote and crossed out 'β≤i' under the union, and the next page repairs this via I*_β.

Condition (c) is written loosely: 'transverse' for a map from a boundary piece to a stratum presumably means a submersion or fibration compatible with the B, Σ structures (cf. margin 'ou trans-sou[mission?]'). As stated it does not yet guarantee that p_β is a locally trivial fibration, which is needed for C(p_β) to be a conical neighbourhood.
Notation drift: Σ_{β,α} is introduced as Σ_α|X_β, but in (d) the pairs '(Ẋ_β, Σ_β)' appear with an undefined Σ_β.

ideas.what: Recovering a stratified space from the complement of tubular neighbourhoods of the minimal strata, glued to mapping cylinders of the boundary-to-stratum projections (X = X* ∪_{Ẋ} C(p)).
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / blow-up of stratified spaces; mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods (Thom–Mather control data, Quinn's homotopically stratified sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (statement of the 'déploiement' theorem, no proofs)

ideas.what: Encoding the stratification combinatorics (poset I split as I_0 ⊔ I*, the sets I*_β) together with transversality conditions (a)–(d) on the cut-open data: the 'système de cylindres-bord transversaux'.
ideas.modern_name: Manifold with corners / 'déployé' data with face-to-stratum fibrations (cf. Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's 'unzip', Albin–Melrose resolution)
ideas.where_published: Only sketched in Esquisse; detailed conditions apparently unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit inductive equivalence between stratified spaces with conical control data plus auxiliary transverse structures (B_α, Σ_α) and 'systems of transverse boundary cylinders'. He states precise transversality axioms that the published literature formulates differently (AFT, Verona). The auxiliary (B_α, Σ_α) structures carried through the induction (perhaps boundary or corner data) are not obviously present in later treatments.
missed.quote: syst. de cylindres-bord transversaux ... (a) Les Ẋ_β disjoints (b) Chaque Ẋ_β transverse à (B*_α,Σ*_α) ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historically relevant precursor to the unzipping equivalence of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. Mathematically, though, the step is standard; it is of interest mainly for documenting how Grothendieck intended to prove the déploiement claim of the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard step: cut out conical neighbourhoods of minimal strata and reconstruct via mapping cylinders. The result is announced in the Esquisse and essentially established later by Verona, Quinn and AFT. The only unpublished content is the bookkeeping and axioms.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed 'Γ' in (19) is Grothendieck's 'I.' (cylinder notation I·Ẋ_{i,β}, I·Ḃ_α), as in (16') on the previous page.
Under the union in the X_i formula one reads 'β∈I_0', with a crossed-out 'β≤i' / 'i≥β' beneath it.
Left margin of (19): 'les Ẋ_β disjoints'. Right margin of (20): '⇒ le syst. des (Ẋ_β,…),(B*_α,Σ*_α) est transverse', followed by an annotation like 'ou trans-sou[mission]'.
Over the top of (18) there is a brace labelled 'syst. de cylindres-bord transversaux'.
